correctness.rationale: Neutrality orients the ten complementary tie pairs independently; strict majority on the other layers guarantees monotonicity. If t_i winning triples contain voter i, that voter has t_i swings from size two and t_i from size three; the corresponding probabilities are t_i/16 and t_i/30 and sum_i t_i=30. Thus both indices are equal exactly at t_i=5. For two voters, balance makes the counts of winning triples containing both and avoiding both equal, while complementation makes their sum four; the pair incidence is two. A separate exact enumeration evaluated the two pivotal definitions over all 1024 orientations, matched the twelve words, and reproduced the full shell sequence 12,120,360,380,140,12 and exact extremal lists. It also checked all 66 fair-word pairs (distance multiplicities 4:30, 6:30, 10:6), the crown adjacency with complementary nonedges, and one S6 orbit with stabilizer 60. The order 60 is a stabilizer of an individual winning-triple family, not the automorphism-group order of the abstract crown graph.
residual_risks: This is a full finite census under the specified six-voter hypotheses. A tie-pair edit changes two profiles; the distances are not counts of individual profile changes.

value.rationale: The distance operationalizes the least intervention preserving neutrality and strict-majority outcomes while equalizing two named power indices. A covering-radius bound alone would not tell how often it is tight or which choice patterns require it. The complete profile covers all labeled rules in a small natural case with a classical fair subfamily and identifies exactly the tie-aligned and anti-aligned obstructions. The geometry organizes the fair targets rather than adding significance by re-counting the old design in isolation.
residual_risks: No claim is made about practical election populations, larger electorates or weighted voters.
